name: Danish state sector pay, new salary system, 01.04.2026

provenance.note: Hand-written excerpt: the state scale plus two consultant positions. Region and municipality are separate documents - they differ in base date, regulation factor and pension rate, not in structure.

provenance.locator: p. 5, 'The regulation factor is as of 01.04.2026 factor 1,265085'
p. 6, derived from the published pairs
provenance.note: 261.000 x 1,265085 = 330.187,19 -> published 330.187. Annual figures are whole kroner; the monthly column is the annual divided by 12 and is not itself rounded.

Same arithmetic as Romania: a frozen per-position value times a single system-wide factor. Denmark froze the values at 31.03.2012 and moves the factor; Romania freezes the coefficients and moves the reference value. reference.amount is 1 because the Danish position values are already in kroner.

stat-nyt-loensystem.label: Basic salary scale grades, new salary system

provenance.locator: p. 6, 'Basic salary for employees in the new salary system'
provenance.note: Each scale grade equals one year of seniority except grade 4, which is two. Grade 3 does not exist in this table. Which grades a person walks depends on their qualification, so the path lives on the position, not on the ladder.

provenance.locator: p. 6, 'Availability supplement for group contract employed administrative officers'
provenance.note: A second, independent seniority ladder attached to a supplement rather than to the base. The reason ladders are a keyed collection and not a single field.

provenance.locator: p. 6, footnote: 'Ingineers, except MScs in Food Science & Technology, are placed in salary grades 4 - 8'

provenance.note: The position value equals its entry step. Written out so a position always carries a value even when the ladder supplies the rest.

provenance.locator: p. 6, footnote: 'Bachelors are placed in grades 1,2,4,4,5'
provenance.note: Grade 4 appears twice - the person stays two years on the same rung. A ladder path with repeats, not a set of steps.

provenance.locator: p. 7, 'Basic salary interval for special and senior consultants'
provenance.note: No seniority ladder: the position is an interval and the point inside it is negotiated. Structurally the same object as a Romanian conducere position with grad managerial I-II set by the head of institution (Art. 10 alin. (7)).

provenance.locator: p. 7, Specialist consultant minimum / maximum, basic amounts 31.03.2012
p. 7, 'Senior Consultant with Personnel Responsibility', basic salary

supplements.name: Supplement for special and senior consultants in the ministries

provenance.note: Supplement tables keep two decimals where the basic salary scale rounds to whole kroner. Hence the per-item rounding override.

provenance.locator: p. 7, 'Supplement for special and senior consultants in the ministries', basic amount 31.03.2012 = 20.000
provenance.note: An absolute amount in the same frozen units as a position value, so it passes through the same reference multiplication: 20.000 x 1,265085 = 25.301,70 as published. Danish supplements are amounts; Romanian ones are percentages. Same field family, different member.

supplements.name: Availability supplement, group contract administrative officers

provenance.note: Amount shown is the entry rung; the supplement escalates along its own ladder 'raadighedstillaeg', independent of the base salary scale.
Applied to the netted basic salary and added on top: 330.187 x 18,07% = 59.664,8 -> 59.665, gross 389.852. 'Netted' here means excluding the employee's own pension contribution, not net of tax.

limitations.text: IDA's tables carry no tax schedule: no AM-bidrag, no bundskat, no kommuneskat, no personfradrag. Net pay is therefore not computed for this regime and payslip.net is null. Inventing Danish tax rates would breach the rule that every number names its source.
Employees may divert pension contributions above 15% to a savings account or take them as pay. Two people on the same rung can therefore show different gross figures for reasons no table records.
The Danish state agreement has no counterpart to Article 21's 20% supplement ceiling. caps is empty, and that emptiness is itself a structural finding rather than missing data.

The new salary system's qualification, function and performance supplements are agreed locally and are not published in any table. What is modelled here is the floor, not what people are paid. Any comparison of Danish dispersion against Romanian dispersion understates the Danish figure.
RON and DKK amounts must never be placed side by side. This regime exists to be compared on shape - ladder form, supplement share, dispersion, who sets what - not on level.
